clue.text: Newly-wed fit for prison?

parts.note: a newly-wed woman is a bride
fit means healthy, well

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a newly married person is fit enough to be sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A BRIDEWELL was an old name for a house of correction, after the London prison near St Bride's Well.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a historic London jail whose name became a general term for a lock-up.

clue.text: Ask for some more questions

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to put a few more questions.
explanation.definitionFit: To request something is to ask politely for it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The top game

parts.note: a game played with a spinning toy like a top, thrown and caught on a string between two sticks

explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling pastime using an hourglass-shaped spinning top on a cord.

clue.text: Artist giving a tune

definitions.meaning: one who produces a tune by blowing through pursed lips

explanation.definitionFit: Whistler was a famous painter, and anyone piping a melody through the lips is also so named.

clue.text: Vehicle it is against the law to leave in the country

definitions.meaning: a curtained couch carried on poles, an old form of transport

definitions.text: it is against the law to leave in the country
definitions.meaning: rubbish dropped in public places, which is an offence

explanation.definitionFit: A carried couch for a passenger, and also discarded rubbish strewn in public places.

clue.text: It produces a whirl of activity in thekitchen

definitions.text: It produces a whirl of activity in thekitchen

parts.words: It produces a whirl of activity in thekitchen
parts.note: a household appliance that spins wet washing round fast to remove water

explanation.definitionFit: A domestic machine that rotates laundry at speed to extract moisture.

clue.text: Church worker in car sits out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A church official is sitting in a parked car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrist is a sacristan, the official who looks after a church's vestments and vessels.

clue.text: Science used by shopkeeper, short time back

parts.note: a chemist keeps a pharmacy shop

indicators.note: back tells us the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: time shortened: year is abbreviated to yr

explanation.surface: A pharmacist used some science a little while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns YR (year shortened) into RY. A chemist in Britain is a pharmacist's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry is the branch of science dealing with substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Accuse one member of taking every one

parts.note: the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
every one means each

explanation.surface: A politician is charged with taking a bribe from everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to bring a formal charge against an official.

clue.text: Mean to have the Italian back in team

indicators.note: in places the turned article inside the team word

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: back means the Italian article is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone intends to bring an Italian player back into the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'in' are the two indicators; the printed 'tea' is an OCR slip for 'team'. 'Mean' looks like a verb (intend) but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid and mean both describe shabby, wretched surroundings.

clue.text: One is never pleased to fly into one

definitions.text: One is never pleased to fly into one

parts.words: One is never pleased to fly into one
parts.note: fly into one sounds like travel but is the idiom for losing your temper in a fit of rage

explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a fit of bad temper, which one flies into, never contentedly.

clue.text: Are without a drink a very long time in journalistic manner

indicators.note: without tells us the named letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone goes for ages without a drink, writing like a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from ARE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news, the style of a journalist's writing.

clue.text: Georgia was violent having parked the car

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state Georgia
raged means stormed violently

explanation.surface: A violent woman named Georgia stormed after parking.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is put away in a lock-up building when it is stored there for the night.

clue.text: Not the places for relaxing one's legs

definitions.text: Not the places for relaxing one's legs

parts.words: Not the places for relaxing one's legs
parts.note: the supports on a chair are for resting the upper limbs, not the lower ones

explanation.definitionFit: These chair supports rest the elbows and forearms, so they are not footstools.

clue.text: Walked round Dorset

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone went on a walk around the county of Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges DORSET. Dorset is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode is the past tense of stride, walking with long steps.

clue.text: The limit for one going down in the world?

definitions.text: The limit for one going down in the world?

parts.words: The limit for one going down in the world?
parts.note: going down sounds like social decline but means heading south on a map, to the planet's furthest point

explanation.definitionFit: The southernmost point of the Earth is as far as a traveller heading south can go.

clue.text: It should give an impression of today

definitions.text: It should give an impression of today

parts.words: It should give an impression of today
parts.note: an impression is an inked mark pressed onto paper, here showing the current day

explanation.definitionFit: A rubber stamp that prints the day's calendar details on documents.

clue.text: Order a cooker as stated

indicators.note: as stated says the words are spoken and heard rather than written

parts.note: a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Someone orders a new kitchen stove, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as stated' says A RANGE, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in order.

clue.text: Tribe carried on with restless wanderer

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A tribe went on its way with a restless nomad.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone who flits from place to place in search of fun.

clue.text: How an unsuccessful tight rope walker might decline

definitions.text: How an unsuccessful tight rope walker might decline

parts.words: How an unsuccessful tight rope walker might decline
parts.note: decline means diminish, but a performer on a high wire who fails drops from it

explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to drop away, and a failing high-wire performer drops from the wire.

clue.text: Main channel of skill by east ern railway

parts.note: art means skill
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A main line built with skill beside an eastern railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a major route or channel, like a main road or blood vessel.

clue.text: Tiresome Edward promises to pay

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A man named Edward keeps writing IOUs, which is tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means wearisome and dull.

clue.text: Hot day in a resort it turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are turned over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: It proved to be a sweltering day at the seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a scorchingly hot day, an informal usage.

clue.text: Cross state while others rest outside

indicators.note: outside places the rearranged letters around the word for state
others suggests a different arrangement of the following word

parts.note: rearranged to TRSE
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: An angry state of mind while the rest relax outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the container signal. 'Cross' looks like angry, but means go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or through an area.

clue.text: Another support

definitions.meaning: one more, as in a further helping
to back a motion or a proposal

explanation.definitionFit: A further one of something, and to back a proposal formally at a meeting.

clue.text: Two boys referring to an early part of the twentieth century

definitions.text: referring to an early part of the twentieth century

parts.note: Edward is a boy's name
Ian is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads are discussing the early 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: The reign of Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, gives its name to that period.

clue.text: Prudent, well-mannered for the most part and in charge

indicators.note: for the most part means only most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: polite means well-mannered

explanation.surface: A sensible person is courteous most of the time and in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of POLITE, leaving POLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means shrewd and sensible, as in a wise course of action.

clue.text: To start, Ronald went to the city

parts.note: Ron is a short form of Ronald

explanation.surface: First of all, Ronald made his way into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start' just puts TO at the front; 'went' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: He may give others a rise in the shop

definitions.text: He may give others a rise in the shop

parts.words: He may give others a rise in the shop
parts.note: a rise sounds like a pay increase, but here it is a ride up between floors of a department store

explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who operated an elevator, carrying shoppers up and down floors.

clue.text: Make a hole in one's attempt at orthodontics perhaps

parts.note: to dent is to make a hollow in something
one is I, and one's is I's, giving IS
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A dentist tries out drilling as part of straightening teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodontics, straightening teeth, is one branch of the dental profession.
